metaData.originalTitle: ChatGPT 将迎来史上最大改版，“AI 只用来聊天的时代结束了”
metaData.title: ChatGPT to Undergo Biggest-Ever Redesign: "The Era of AI for Chatting Alone Is Over"
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: OpenAI plans to integrate its coding tool Codex into ChatGPT, transforming it into a super app capable of writing code, managing schedules, and controlling software, marking a strategic shift from a chatbot to an AI agent platform.
metaData.summary: Based on exclusive reporting from the Financial Times, the article details OpenAI's largest redesign of ChatGPT since its 2022 launch. The core change involves integrating Codex, its fastest-growing programming tool, into ChatGPT and connecting it with external partner applications. The analysis unfolds across four dimensions: strategic intent, technological foundation, competitive pressure, and business logic. OpenAI executives believe the future of AI lies in agents that execute tasks for users, not simple conversations. The upgrade of the underlying GPT-5.5 model enables Codex to independently perform complex, multi-step tasks. Anthropic's Claude Code, which previously led OpenAI in coding capabilities, directly prompted OpenAI to rapidly form a Codex team and restructure its organization. With an IPO approaching, OpenAI needs to push Codex to its 900 million consumer users to drive willingness to pay. The article also notes that Codex's desktop app saw its user base grow sixfold in two months, surpassing 5 million weekly active users, and details OpenAI's decision to shelve consumer businesses like Sora to concentrate resources on enterprise clients.

mainPoints.point: ChatGPT will transition from a chatbot to a super app, with the core being the integration of the coding tool Codex.
mainPoints.explanation: OpenAI plans to fully integrate Codex into ChatGPT and connect it with external partner applications, enabling it to write code, manage schedules, and control software, becoming an agent platform that executes tasks for users.

mainPoints.point: The upgrade of the underlying GPT-5.5 model is a key driver of Codex's capability leap.
mainPoints.explanation: GPT-5.5 is significantly better than its predecessor at handling long, multi-step tasks, requiring less frequent human guidance. This allows Codex to execute independently after receiving clear instructions, increasing developer trust.

mainPoints.point: Anthropic's Claude Code taking the lead was the direct catalyst for OpenAI's accelerated integration.
mainPoints.explanation: In the fall of 2024, Anthropic's coding capabilities surpassed OpenAI's. After releasing the Claude Code preview in February 2025, OpenAI quickly formed a Codex team and restructured its organization, merging the ChatGPT, Codex, and API teams.

mainPoints.point: With an IPO approaching, OpenAI needs to push Codex to its 900 million consumer users to drive willingness to pay.
mainPoints.explanation: Codex users are mostly paid subscribers with high monetization efficiency. OpenAI has shelved consumer businesses like Sora to concentrate resources on enterprise clients, aiming to solidify its revenue data before going public.

mainPoints.point: Directly writing code is more efficient than simulating human browser operations, positioning Codex as the core of a general-purpose agent.
mainPoints.explanation: OpenAI previously launched Operator to have AI simulate human actions in a browser, but it was too inefficient. Executives believe directly writing code is a more effective approach, aligning with Anthropic's path from Claude Code to Claude Cowork.

keyQuotes: The era of AI being used only for chatting is over.
With an agent that can do anything for you on your computer, the next goal is to push this capability to everyone.
By GPT-5.5, Codex's advantage had become too significant to ignore.
Directly writing code is a more effective way for AI to accomplish tasks on a computer, such as building complex spreadsheets.
Will the hundreds of millions of consumers accustomed to free 'chit-chat' and conversation ultimately be willing to pay for a digital agent that can work for them and help them earn a living?

relatedArticles.title: A Serious Discussion: How Much of Our Skills Can Skill Actually Distill? | Hao's Trend Talk
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article delves into the capability boundaries of AI Agent Skills, pointing out that while they excel at encoding explicit rules and knowledge routing, they cannot capture the tacit intuition and utility judgment that human experts rely on in complex decision-making.

relatedArticles.title: Harness Is Not the Goal, Knowledge Is the Moat — Knowledge Accumulation Practices of an AI Engineering Delivery Team
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Based on the engineering delivery practices of an AI Team, this article proposes that knowledge accumulation is more important than workflow orchestration, and systematically introduces a complete methodology encompassing a five-layer knowledge storage architecture, a three-level maturity system, and how workflows serve knowledge accumulation.

relatedArticles.title: Understanding Harness Engineering: Finding the Shell That Keeps AI from Going Rogue—Insights from 14 Engineering Articles | Hao's Trend Talk
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of "Harness Engineering," a core technology in the AI Agent field. It reveals how to compensate for model shortcomings through a three-layer management architecture and proposes the logic of "Compensation Surface Migration" that evolves with model capabilities.

relatedArticles.title: Understanding Hermes in One Article: How the New Top-Tier Agent Self-Evolves from Experience
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of the core innovation of the Hermes Agent—the Skills closed-loop system—detailing its complete implementation mechanism, from experience extraction and knowledge storage to intelligent retrieval and self-improvement, along with its engineering trade-offs and security considerations.

relatedArticles.title: Investing 10,000 RMB in AI: A Year of Tools, Practices, and Reflections
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: A systematic summary of a veteran developer's practical experience in the AI wave, covering everything from MAC toolchain optimization and Harness Engineering architectural constraints to building an Agent-driven automated learning loop.

relatedArticles.title: In the AI-Induced Cognitive Disarmament, We Will Lose More Than Just Ability | Hao Chat on Trends
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: From the perspectives of cognitive psychology, labor sociology, and philosophy, this article systematically argues that the 'cognitive disarmament' brought about by AI is not a simple degradation of abilities, but a historic turning point where alienation has deepened from the labor process to the thought generation process, rooted in the growth society's endless pursuit of efficiency.

relatedArticles.title: Why Did Hermes Take Over from OpenClaw in Just Two Months?
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth comparison between the rising open-source AI Agent star Hermes and its predecessor OpenClaw, arguing that Hermes' success stems not from functional superiority but from encapsulating decision complexity—such as skill auto-evolution and proactive memory management—within underlying deterministic rules. This engineering safety net allowed it to deliver an automated 'gets better with use' experience precisely when the underlying technology was just barely sufficient.

relatedArticles.title: Harness Engineering: How I Spent a Week Boosting AI Coding Rate to 90% in an Enterprise App
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article systematically introduces Harness Engineering, a new AI coding paradigm that elevates the AI code rate of an enterprise Java application from 25% to over 90% by building a four-element system of rules, skills, knowledge, and change management.

relatedArticles.title: Q1 2026: AI Agents Come of Age | 2026 Q1 AI Trend White Paper
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of four structural trends in AI Agents for Q1 2026: long-horizon productization, harness engineering, recursive R&D, and the Skill ecosystem, revealing the flywheel effect as Agents evolve from tools into independent 'new colleagues'.

relatedArticles.title: What You Don't Know About Claude Code: Architecture, Governance, and Engineering Practices - Tw93
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of Claude Code's six-layer architecture and engineering practices, proposing a systematic Agent development methodology from context governance and skill design to a verification loop.
